youtube.title: 🔥 This 15MB App Connects to 50+ Databases
youtube.description:
Tired of juggling DBeaver, TablePlus, and three other database tools just to manage your stack? DBX is a 15MB database client built with Rust that connects to MySQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, ClickHouse, and 46 other databases in one tiny app. No Java runtime bloat. No platform lock-in. Just download, install, and connect.

What makes DBX special? It has a built-in AI assistant that writes SQL for you right inside the editor. Highlight a table, describe what you need in plain language, and get production-ready SQL with built-in safety checks. It works with Claude, OpenAI, or local models.

DBX also speaks the Model Context Protocol, so AI coding agents like Claude Code, Cursor, and Windsurf can query your databases through connections you already set up. One config, everywhere.

With nearly 5,000 stars on GitHub, DBX runs on macOS, Windows, and Linux. You can even self-host it with Docker for team access. The web version gives you the same feature set in the browser.

Next time you need to debug a production query across three different databases, skip the tool-switching headache. Just open DBX.

Repo link in description. Follow for more project updates that actually help you build.

linkedin.text:
I spent years switching between DBeaver, TablePlus, and command-line clients just to manage different databases. Every new project meant installing another tool, dealing with Java dependencies, or being locked into one platform.

Then I found DBX.

It's a 15MB database client that connects to MySQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, ClickHouse, and 46 other databases. Built with Rust and Tauri, it's fast, lightweight, and runs on macOS, Windows, and Linux without any runtime bloat.

But here's what really got me: DBX has a built-in AI assistant that writes SQL for you. You highlight a table, describe what you need in plain language, and it generates production-ready SQL with safety checks. It works with Claude, OpenAI, or local models via Ollama.

Even better? It speaks the Model Context Protocol. That means AI coding agents like Claude Code, Cursor, and Windsurf can query your databases through connections you already configured in DBX. No more copy-pasting credentials or switching contexts.

With nearly 5,000 stars on GitHub and active development, DBX is becoming my go-to database tool. You can self-host it with Docker for team access, or use the web version in browser-only environments.

If you're tired of tool sprawl and want one clean interface for all your databases, check out DBX. Link in the comments.
